objective: Prove, for the infinite CNF on all names of F2 = <x, y>: (1) the board states are exactly the right congruences, i.e. the subgroups H of F2 with their Schreier graphs, and on the ball B_L the restrictions of right congruences (folded quotients of the ball); (2) refinement: if no clause has a positive identity literal besides the board axioms, refining an allowed board keeps it allowed, so the tree is allowed whenever any state is; (3) unfolding: for a law over a finite alphabet whose every identity literal relates the same offset of two base names (it names no relation), if some allowed state has an infinite board then some allowed state has the tree as its board, so no such law forces an infinite board; (4) every finite board is forced by some law that names no relation; (5) two different boards differ in infinitely many identity distinctions and every place of a board other than the tree holds infinitely many names, so no distinction of such a state is flipped by a change of finitely many variables; (6) for value laws, the collapse is allowed iff a constant colouring is allowed iff every board is allowed; (7) identity of indiscernibles at radius r makes every board finite (at most q^|B_r| places), at radius 1 with one bit the boards are the balanced view sets, and every law with a plane-like abelian board there also has a non-abelian one; (8) naming one relation suffices: the commutator rule e(u, u x y X Y) with an aperiodic Wang-tile law forces exactly the plane. Or record which statement fails and why.
status: Proved 2026-11-10: with names the reduced words of F2 and e(u, v) an identity distinction per pair (transitivity, letter closure, constancy), the boards are exactly the Schreier graphs of subgroups of F2; refinement keeps a state allowed when no clause has a positive identity literal beyond the board axioms; unfolding: a law that names no relation (same offset on both sides of every identity literal) and allows an infinite board allows the tree, so no such law forces the plane or any infinite board; every finite board can be forced; two boards differ in infinitely many identity distinctions and off the tree every place holds infinitely many names, so no distinction there is flipped by a finite change; the collapse lemma; identity of indiscernibles makes boards finite, with the radius-1 swap; the commutator rule with an aperiodic tile law forces exactly the plane. Finite checks passed (check.py).
title: Boards of laws that name no relation
